description: We’re a team of CSE students from Kerala participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 .. We’re into tech, AI, web dev, and space, and we’re excited to build something creative and useful with NASA’s data. Here to learn, experiment, and make something cool together...
summary:
Martian Mission Planner is an intelligent route-planning prototype designed to help astronauts navigate the challenging terrain of Mars. Instead of relying on the shortest straight-line path, it aims to identify routes that balance travel distance, time, and terrain safety.

The application features an interactive Mars map where users can select starting points and destinations using geographic coordinates. It incorporates NASA's Mars elevation data (MOLA) as the foundation for terrain analysis, including elevation mapping, slope calculation, and identification of potential geological hazards such as craters, depressions, and steep regions.

By combining terrain information with configurable mission safety constraints and pathfinding algorithms such as A*, the system aims to recommend safer and more efficient routes. This project addresses the importance of reliable surface navigation for future human exploration, helping astronauts make informed decisions while reducing exposure to difficult terrain.
details:
Martian Mission Planner is an interactive Mars exploration and navigation platform designed to help plan safer and more efficient surface journeys for future astronauts.

How it works:
Users can select a starting location and destination on an interactive map of Mars using latitude and longitude coordinates. The application calculates the distance between these locations and provides a foundation for terrain-aware route planning. Our proposed terrain module uses NASA's Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) elevation data to analyse the Martian surface. By processing elevation data and calculating slope, the system aims to identify difficult terrain, including steep slopes, craters, depressions, and elevated regions. We plan to incorporate A* pathfinding to generate routes that account for terrain conditions rather than simply following the shortest straight-line distance.

Benefits and intended impact:
The project aims to support mission planning by helping astronauts and mission planners evaluate terrain challenges before travelling across the Martian surface. It could reduce exposure to hazardous terrain, improve travel efficiency, and help identify routes that also offer scientific exploration opportunities. Ultimately, it contributes to the development of intelligent navigation tools for future human missions to Mars.

Technology used:

  • Frontend: React.js, JavaScript, HTML, CSS and Tailwind CSS.
  • Mapping: Leaflet and React Leaflet.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Data processing: NumPy, with raster-processing tools planned for DEM analysis.
  • Scientific data: NASA MOLA elevation datasets.
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code and Git.

Creativity and innovation:
The central idea is to treat Martian navigation as a multi-factor decision-making problem rather than a simple distance calculation. A geographically shorter route may cross steep slopes or deep depressions, while a slightly longer route may be considerably more suitable for a mission. Our approach combines terrain analysis, configurable safety constraints, and intelligent pathfinding to address this problem.

Factors considered:
Our team considers elevation, slope, surface obstacles, travel distance, estimated travel time, temperature, radiation exposure, atmospheric conditions, and scientifically interesting locations. We also recognise that global elevation datasets have resolution limitations, so detailed local terrain data would be valuable for more precise navigation.

Martian Mission Planner aims to bridge planetary science and intelligent route planning, turning scientific terrain information into practical decisions for future Mars exploration.
